source.schemaGeneration: z.toJSONSchema exported Zod schemas; npm dependencies installed under blackwall/

groups.title: Identity and mode
groups.description: Active policy identifier, version, and operating mode.

groups.title: Profiles and risk responses
groups.description: Semantic-evaluation thresholds and default responses to uncertainty.

groups.title: Approvals and denials
groups.description: Conditions for user approval and behavior after a denial.

groups.title: Tool and data scope
groups.description: Limits on operations, files, network access, shell use, and budgets.

groups.title: Topics and supervision
groups.description: Catalog of topics, topic policies, embeddings, and the guardian.

groups.title: Models and costs
groups.description: Model aliases, context limits, and rates used for cost budgets.

fields.title: Schema version
fields.description: Configuration schema version; the loader currently accepts only version 1.
fields.effect: An invalid version causes the configuration to be rejected.

evidence.note: Based on the schema and runtime code; there is no dedicated demo clip for this field.

fields.title: Policy identifier
fields.description: Stable name for this policy in configuration and audit records.
fields.effect: Appears in audit context.
fields.limits: Any non-empty text; the schema does not enforce this.

evidence.note: Based on the schema and runtime code; there is no dedicated demo clip for this field.

fields.title: Active policy version
fields.description: Policy version counter. Runtime publication increments it after checking expected_version.
fields.effect: Helps detect version conflicts during publication.
fields.limits: Positive integer; cannot be edited directly.

evidence.note: Original Polish recording: shows runtime publication; the run summary confirms version v3.

fields.title: Enforcement mode
fields.description: `enforce` applies denials; `observe` records some soft denials as observations.
fields.effect: In `enforce`, a denial blocks the operation. In `observe`, some denials are recorded as observed; hard blocks still apply.

evidence.note: Based on the schema and runtime code; there is no dedicated demo clip for this field.

fields.title: Active profile
fields.description: Selects a set of thresholds and responses from `profiles`.
fields.effect: Used for semantic evaluations and content checks.

evidence.note: Based on the schema and runtime code; there is no dedicated demo clip for this field.

fields.title: Semantic evaluation scope
fields.description: Specifies which non-shell operation classes require an additional Jev review. Every allowed shell call is reviewed regardless.
fields.effect: Applies to the selected profile; affects semantic evaluation and output checks.

evidence.note: Original Polish recording: Jev evaluates a shell request; the other options are code configuration.

fields.title: Minimum allow probability
fields.description: Minimum probability required to accept a Jev response.
fields.effect: Applies to the selected profile; affects semantic evaluation and output checks.

evidence.note: The original Polish UI recording illustrates runtime publication; it does not show this specific threshold being changed. The verification summary confirms a 400/409 conflict response.

fields.title: Minimum evaluation confidence
fields.description: Minimum Jev confidence. Results below this confidence follow `on_uncertain`.
fields.effect: Applies to the selected profile; affects semantic evaluation and output checks.

evidence.note: Original Polish recording: Jev evaluates a shell request; the other options are code configuration.

fields.title: Secret handling
fields.description: `block` rejects detected secrets; `redact` masks them before further processing.
fields.effect: Applies to the selected profile; affects semantic evaluation and output checks.

evidence.note: Original Polish recording: Jev evaluates a shell request; the other options are code configuration.

fields.title: Personal data handling
fields.description: `off` disables PII scanning; `redact` masks detected data; `block` rejects it.
fields.effect: Applies to the selected profile; affects semantic evaluation and output checks.

evidence.note: Original Polish recording: Jev evaluates a shell request; the other options are code configuration.

fields.title: Response to uncertain evaluations
fields.description: Chooses whether to deny or request approval when semantic evaluation is inconclusive.
fields.effect: Applies to the selected profile; determines the response to an uncertain result.

evidence.note: Original Polish recording: Jev evaluates a shell request; the other options are code configuration.

fields.title: Default effect
fields.description: The policy requires denial as the default effect; no alternative value is supported.
fields.effect: Unknown or unapproved operations are denied by default.

evidence.note: Based on the schema and runtime code; there is no dedicated demo clip for this field.

fields.title: Session state after denial
fields.description: Determines whether a standard denial blocks the session or allows it to continue.
fields.effect: `block` blocks the session; `continue` permits further requests subject to policy.

evidence.note: Based on the schema and runtime code; there is no dedicated demo clip for this field.

fields.title: Correction-eligible reason codes
fields.description: Reason codes for which the system may ask for a corrected request.
fields.effect: May start the correction flow for the specified denials.
fields.limits: List of reason codes; an empty `[]` is allowed.

evidence.note: Based on the schema and runtime code; there is no dedicated demo clip for this field.

fields.title: Maximum correction attempts
fields.description: Maximum number of attempts to correct a denied request.
fields.effect: No further corrections are accepted through this flow once the limit is reached.

evidence.note: Based on the schema and runtime code; there is no dedicated demo clip for this field.

fields.title: Approvals enabled
fields.description: Allows approval requests where a rule permits that effect.
fields.effect: When disabled, an operation requiring approval cannot proceed through this flow.

evidence.note: Based on the schema and runtime code; there is no dedicated demo clip for this field.

fields.title: Approval-eligible reason codes
fields.description: Explicit allowlist of reason codes eligible for an approval request.
fields.effect: Core creates an approval request only when `approvals.enabled=true` and every required reason is on this list; otherwise, it denies the request.
fields.limits: Does not override hard denials (`HARD`), including session state, exhausted budgets, or unavailable guardian, judge, or embeddings. API authentication is checked earlier; this list does not replace it.

evidence.note: Based on the schema and runtime code; there is no dedicated demo clip for this field.

fields.title: Approval TTL
fields.description: Number of seconds before a pending approval expires.
fields.effect: When approval expires, the session is blocked and the operation is not executed.

evidence.note: Based on the schema and runtime code; there is no dedicated demo clip for this field.

fields.title: Allowed tools
fields.description: Tools available within this scope.
fields.effect: A tool request outside the effective allowlist is denied.
fields.limits: Tool allowlist; intersected with `deny` and the global scope.

evidence.note: Original Polish recordings show selected enforcement examples; the gateway code defines the details.

fields.title: Denied tools
fields.description: Tools explicitly disabled within this scope.
fields.effect: A request for the specified tool is denied.
fields.limits: Denials take precedence; the user scope combines with the global scope.

evidence.note: Original Polish recordings show selected enforcement examples; the gateway code defines the details.

fields.title: Allowed read roots
fields.description: Paths from which files may be read or listed. The same restriction may appear in a user configuration (`users.*.files.read_roots`) and narrow the global scope.
fields.effect: Reads outside the allowed scope are denied.
fields.limits: Effective `read_roots` are the intersection of `global.files` and `users.*.files`; user roots can narrow access.

evidence.note: Original Polish recordings show selected enforcement examples; the gateway code defines the details.

fields.title: Allowed write roots
fields.description: Paths where files may be created or modified.
fields.effect: Writes outside the allowed scope are denied.
fields.limits: The user scope narrows the global scope.

evidence.note: Original Polish recordings show selected enforcement examples; the gateway code defines the details.

fields.title: Denied file basenames
fields.description: Basenames of files on which operations are prohibited.
fields.effect: Operations on a listed basename are denied.

evidence.note: Original Polish recordings show selected enforcement examples; the gateway code defines the details.

fields.title: Allowed file extensions
fields.description: File extensions accepted for file access.
fields.effect: Other extensions fail the file-access check.
fields.limits: Include the leading dot, following the application’s convention.

evidence.note: Original Polish recordings show selected enforcement examples; the gateway code defines the details.

fields.title: Reject symlinks
fields.description: Rejects paths that contain symbolic links.
fields.effect: Prevents traversal through symbolic links.

evidence.note: Original Polish recordings show selected enforcement examples; the gateway code defines the details.

fields.title: File size limit
fields.description: Maximum file size for reads and maximum proposed write or edit size, in bytes.
fields.effect: Reads of files larger than this limit are denied. Writes are checked against the content byte length; edits are checked against a conservative estimate of the resulting file size before execution.
fields.limits: Positive integer. The edit estimate may retain unmatched old text, so it can exceed the eventual file size. This limit does not make opening or writing a file atomic.

evidence.note: Original Polish recordings show selected enforcement examples; the gateway code defines the details.

fields.title: Roots requiring approval
fields.description: Writing an existing file in these locations requires approval.
fields.effect: May create a pending approval request before a write.
fields.limits: Directories and files beneath the listed roots.

evidence.note: Original Polish recordings show selected enforcement examples; the gateway code defines the details.

fields.title: Allowed URL schemes
fields.description: Protocol schemes accepted by the HTTP gateway.
fields.effect: Other URL schemes are denied.
fields.limits: For example, `https`; address validation is separate.

evidence.note: Original Polish recordings show selected enforcement examples; the gateway code defines the details.

fields.title: Allowed hosts
fields.description: Hosts to which requests may be sent.
fields.effect: A host outside the list is denied.
fields.limits: The user list is intersected with the global list.

evidence.note: Original Polish recordings show selected enforcement examples; the gateway code defines the details.

fields.title: Allow subdomains
fields.description: Allows matching subdomains of hosts in `allow_hosts`.
fields.effect: Extends host matching according to gateway rules.

evidence.note: Original Polish recordings show selected enforcement examples; the gateway code defines the details.

fields.title: Allowed ports
fields.description: Port numbers allowed in requests.
fields.effect: A port outside the list is denied.
fields.limits: Integers; runtime validates the valid port range.

evidence.note: Original Polish recordings show selected enforcement examples; the gateway code defines the details.

fields.title: Allowed HTTP methods
fields.description: HTTP methods accepted within this scope.
fields.effect: Disallowed methods are denied.

evidence.note: Original Polish recordings show selected enforcement examples; the gateway code defines the details.

fields.title: Block non-public IPs
fields.description: Requires the host’s resolved IP addresses to be public.
fields.effect: A non-public address is denied after DNS resolution.

evidence.note: Original Polish recordings show selected enforcement examples; the gateway code defines the details.

fields.title: Follow redirects
fields.description: Configures how the HTTP executor handles redirects.
fields.effect: Controls behavior after a redirect response.

evidence.note: Original Polish recordings show selected enforcement examples; the gateway code defines the details.

fields.title: Allowed URL paths
fields.description: Path prefixes permitted on an allowed host.
fields.effect: A path outside the list is denied.
fields.limits: Exact match or a descendant path.

evidence.note: Original Polish recordings show selected enforcement examples; the gateway code defines the details.

fields.title: Test-fixture exceptions
fields.description: Exact host:port pairs exempt from non-public IP blocking. The schema comment marks them as test-only.
fields.effect: The exception skips the public-IP check for the matching pair.
fields.limits: Use only with controlled fixtures; this is not a host allowlist.

evidence.note: Original Polish recordings show selected enforcement examples; the gateway code defines the details.

fields.title: Session token budget
fields.description: Maximum number of tokens reserved and spent in a session.
fields.effect: Budget-dependent actions are blocked once the limit is reached.

evidence.note: Original Polish recordings show selected enforcement examples; the gateway code defines the details.

fields.title: Tool-attempt budget
fields.description: Maximum number of tool-call attempts in a session.
fields.effect: Further attempts are denied once the limit is exhausted.

evidence.note: Original Polish recordings show selected enforcement examples; the gateway code defines the details.

fields.title: Model-request budget
fields.description: Maximum number of model requests in a session.
fields.effect: Further model requests are blocked once the limit is reached.

evidence.note: Original Polish recordings show selected enforcement examples; the gateway code defines the details.

fields.title: Session time limit
fields.description: Maximum elapsed wall-clock time for a session, in seconds.
fields.effect: The session cannot continue after exceeding the limit.

evidence.note: Original Polish recordings show selected enforcement examples; the gateway code defines the details.

fields.title: Cost limit (micro-USD)
fields.description: Maximum session cost, expressed in millionths of a US dollar.
fields.effect: Runtime blocks costs it cannot price; model aliases need rates.

evidence.note: Original Polish recordings show selected enforcement examples; the gateway code defines the details.

fields.title: Tool timeout
fields.description: Maximum timeout for a single tool operation.
fields.effect: The executor receives a timeout no greater than the configured limit.

evidence.note: Original Polish recordings show selected enforcement examples; the gateway code defines the details.

fields.title: Enable shell
fields.description: Enables the `bash` tool within this scope.
fields.effect: Shell requests are denied when the shell is disabled.

evidence.note: Original Polish recordings show selected enforcement examples; the gateway code defines the details.

fields.title: Maximum command size
fields.description: Maximum shell command length, in bytes.
fields.effect: Larger commands are denied.

evidence.note: Original Polish recordings show selected enforcement examples; the gateway code defines the details.

fields.title: Shell timeout
fields.description: Maximum time allowed for a command to run.
fields.effect: The executor terminates a command when the limit expires.

evidence.note: Original Polish recordings show selected enforcement examples; the gateway code defines the details.

fields.title: Execution profile
fields.description: Selects the shell execution profile declared in the configuration.
fields.effect: `isolated` is a declared profile value. When `require_isolation=true`, runtime checks only that value; it does not detect or create an operating-system sandbox.

evidence.note: Original Polish recordings show selected enforcement examples; the gateway code defines the details.

fields.title: Require the isolated profile
fields.description: Rejects shell operations unless `execution_profile` is set to `isolated`.
fields.effect: Shell requests are denied if this condition is not met.
fields.limits: This checks the declared configuration only; it does not provide an OS sandbox.

evidence.note: Original Polish recordings show selected enforcement examples; the gateway code defines the details.

evidence.note: Original Polish recordings show selected enforcement examples; the gateway code defines the details.

scopeNote: This guide explains configuration fields and behavior visible in the code. JSON Schema validates structure and simple ranges, but does not replace semantic checks for catalog references, existing aliases, runtime threshold consistency, path validity, publication versions, or Jev/guardian semantic evaluation. A topic assigned to a user in configuration is trusted context; embedding detection creates a candidate, and the guardian separately reviews the current event against forbidden and allowed clauses. The `isolated` profile and `require_isolation` declare a configuration requirement, but do not provide an operating-system sandbox. `threat_feed.path` is set at startup; feed contents can be published through the API or UI. Runtime publication cannot change model aliases, providers, database paths, tokens, workdirs, or `topic_ids` assignments. Publishing a complete `topics` catalog requires `topic_policies`. Change objects merge into the active configuration, while arrays in a patch replace existing arrays. `observe` does not disable hard blocks. Central SSO is outside the scope of this schema and guide.
